PT Looping and Leveraged Strategy Risks: The Services include a feature that enables the User to self-direct automated leveraged looping strategies for Principal Tokens ("PT Looping"). PT Looping involves, among other things, supplying PT as collateral to third-party money market protocols, borrowing digital assets (including but not limited to stablecoins) against that collateral, and using the borrowed funds to acquire additional PT to amplify yield exposure. The use of leverage in this manner also amplifies potential losses. Liquidation or solvency of a looped position depends on the relevant risk parameters, including but not limited to the risk parameters you set and/or the parameters applicable to the third-party money market protocol, which the Pendle Group does not operate or control. Users acknowledge and accept all risks associated with PT Looping, including but not limited to: (a) Amplified loss. Losses on the PT position are amplified by the leverage applied; (b) Third-party money market liquidation. The applicable money market protocol may result in automatic liquidation of the User's collateral when the health factor of the looped position falls below its liquidation threshold, irrespective of the User's intent or action; (c) Variable borrowing cost risk. Borrow interest rates on money market protocols are variable and may increase to levels that exceed the PT fixed APY, rendering the looping strategy net-negative; (d) Money market parameter changes. Money market protocols may change their liquidation loan-to-value or other applicable thresholds, collateral factors, or eligible collateral through their own governance or administrative processes at any time without prior notice, including in relation to existing positions, which may cause a position that would otherwise have remained solvent to become subject to liquidation; (e) PT collateral valuation risk. A PT Looping strategy may increase exposure to smart contract vulnerabilities, operational failures, and oracle risks across Pendle and each third-party protocol involved, by virtue of leverage involved. Where a significant number of users hold looped positions in the same PT market, a sharp decline in PT price or widening of the PT discount may trigger simultaneous liquidations across multiple positions, which may cause reflexive downward price pressure on PT and further cascade liquidations. The risk of cascade is also amplified where the aggregate size of leveraged positions in one or more third-party money markets significantly exceeds the liquidity available; and (h) Automated execution risk. Boros-Specific Risk Factors Boros Eligibility. In addition to the general restrictions on Excluded Persons set out in these Terms, access to and use of Boros is not available to persons who are citizens of, resident in, or located in the United States of America (including its territories and possessions). Users located in the United States of America are prohibited from accessing or using Boros, whether directly or through a virtual private network, proxy, or any other method of circumventing this restriction. The following risk factors apply specifically to users of the Boros product. If you do not use Boros, this subsection does not apply to you. (i) Funding Rate Volatility Risk. Funding rates on perpetual markets are highly volatile and can move dramatically and rapidly, including as a result of events entirely unrelated to digital asset markets (such as commodity price shocks, macroeconomic developments, or geopolitical events). Funding rate movements may be sudden, extreme, and unpredictable. Historical funding rate data is not a reliable indicator of future rates. (ii) Extreme Market Event / Black Swan Risk. Pendle expressly draws users' attention to the risk of extreme, low-probability but high-impact market events ("Black Swan Events") that may cause simultaneous, severe dislocations across multiple funding rate markets. Such events may include, without limitation, sudden macro-driven price dislocations, cascading liquidations across the broader derivatives market, or correlated spikes in funding rates across multiple asset classes. In such conditions, users may face losses that materially exceed what they would have anticipated under normal market conditions. (iii) Auto-Deleveraging (ADL) Risk — Boros. ADL is a mechanism built into Boros whereby profitable positions held by certain users may be forcibly reduced or closed without prior notice in order to cover losses arising from positions held by other users whose collateral is insufficient to meet their obligations. ADL can occur during, or as a direct result of, extreme market conditions. It can result in the involuntary closure of a position that would otherwise have remained profitable. ADL can be triggered by the conduct or positions of entirely unrelated third parties. Users acknowledge that ADL is an inherent feature of the Boros risk management system and that the Pendle Group bears no liability for losses arising from an ADL event. (iv) Market Pausing Risk. The Pendle Group reserves the right to pause, suspend, or restrict trading activity on Boros markets front-end in circumstances including, without limitation: (a) detection of a material security vulnerability or active exploit; (b) oracle failure or price feed malfunction; (c) extreme market conditions that, in the Pendle Group's reasonable assessment, threaten the integrity of the protocol or the safety of user funds; or (d) regulatory requirement or order. During any such pause or suspension, users may be unable to open, close, reduce, or hedge their positions. A pause may be implemented at any time without prior notice and may last for an indeterminate period. Losses incurred during a pause period, including losses arising from an inability to exit, reduce, or hedge a position, are borne entirely by the user. The Pendle Group bears no liability for any such losses. (v) Liquidity Risk — Funding Rate Markets. Liquidity in funding rate markets may be limited, particularly during periods of high volatility or at times of low market participation. In periods of low liquidity, the effective cost of entering or exiting a position may be materially higher than expected, and it may be impossible to close a position at an economically rational price. The Pendle Group makes no representation as to the availability of liquidity in any Boros market at any time. (vi) Reference Market and Oracle Risk. Boros settlement calculations are derived from funding rates published by third-party perpetual trading venues (each, a "Reference Market") and transmitted to Boros via an oracle systems (the "Rate Oracle"). The Pendle Group does not operate, control, or have any affiliation with any Reference Market or the Rate Oracle infrastructure of the venues of such Reference Market. Users should be aware of the following risks: (a) Reference Market Manipulation. The funding rate used for Boros settlement may be susceptible to manipulation by third parties acting on a Reference Market. If the published funding rate is artificially distorted, Boros settlement calculations will reflect the manipulated rate. The Pendle Group has no ability to detect, prevent, or reverse the effect of such manipulation on Boros settlements. (b) Reference Market Unavailability. If a Reference Market ceases operations, experiences a technical outage, or suspends publication of funding rate data, the Rate Oracle will have no data to query and Boros settlement may be delayed, disrupted, or suspended. (c) Oracle Transmission Failure. The Rate Oracle itself may experience technical failures or data transmission errors, resulting in Boros contracts receiving stale, delayed, or incorrect rate data. The Pendle Group bears no liability for settlement disruption, position outcomes, or losses arising from any of the foregoing. (vii) Acknowledgement of Global Deleveraging Mechanics. The Pendle Group has published a separate document setting out in detail the mechanics of the global deleveraging system that operates within Boros (the "Boros Deleveraging Disclosure", accessible at https://docs.pendle.finance/boros-docs/adlMechanics). Access to and use of Boros is conditional upon the user having read and understood the Boros Deleveraging Disclosure in full. By accessing or using Boros, you irrevocably confirm that you have: (a) read the Boros Deleveraging Disclosure in its entirety; (b) understood the mechanics of global deleveraging as described therein, including in particular the risk that your open positions may be involuntarily and immediately reduced or closed without prior notice as a result of another user's insolvency; and (c) accepted and agreed to be subject to the global deleveraging system as an inherent and unconditional feature of Boros. If you have not read and understood the Boros Deleveraging Disclosure, you must not access or use Boros. The Pendle Group will implement a confirmation step within the Boros interface requiring users to affirmatively acknowledge receipt and understanding of the Boros Deleveraging Disclosure prior to placing their first order. Completion of that confirmation step constitutes an express acknowledgement of, and agreement to, the global deleveraging mechanics as described in the Boros Deleveraging Disclosure and these Terms. CrossEx Arbitrage Risk Factors The following risk factors apply where you use the Pendle CrossEx Arbitrage Tool (the "Arbitrage Tool"), an open-source application published by the Pendle Group that coordinates a funding rate arbitrage strategy using Boros perpetual positions together with perpetual futures positions on third-party centralised exchanges, including Gate CrossEx, Hyperliquid, and Binance (each, a "Relevant CEX"). The Arbitrage Tool is described as experimental and is provided on an as-is basis. If you do not use the Arbitrage Tool, this sub-section does not apply to you: (a) Delta-neutral does not mean no risk of loss. A strategy described as "delta-neutral" addresses only directional price exposure. It does not eliminate or reduce any other risk. You remain fully exposed to (the following being a non-exhaustive list): (i) liquidation on Boros or on any Relevant CEX, including liquidation caused by margin shortfall, oracle price movement, or funding rate changes; (ii) execution risk where one or more legs fail to fill, leaving net directional or funding exposure until manually corrected; (iii) funding rate movements that are adverse to the held positions; (iv) smart contract, oracle, or operational failure affecting Boros; (v) failure of any Relevant CEX, including insolvency, API outage, or forced position closure; and (vi) any other risk described in these Terms. Until all four legs are in position, you may carry unintended directional or one-sided funding exposure. Partial fills, rejected orders, or delays may result in an unhedged position requiring manual intervention. The Pendle Group does not guarantee simultaneous or coordinated execution of all legs. Liquidation on a Relevant CEX is governed by that Relevant CEX's margin rules and is not controlled by Pendle. (f) Leverage. The Arbitrage Tool deploys notional positions that are typically a multiple of the capital contributed. Leverage amplifies the effect of adverse margin movements, funding rate changes, and liquidation thresholds on both sides of the trade. Liquidation on Boros or on a Relevant CEX may occur independently of the other legs; liquidation of one leg does not automatically close the opposing leg, and an unhedged residual position may remain. It is not an offer, guarantee, or commitment. Rates and prices change continuously; your executed return will differ from any preview, potentially materially. (h) Regulatory access restrictions. Capital Markets Product Token Risk Factors Where the Protocol supports yield-bearing assets that are or include Capital Markets Product Tokens (as defined below), the following additional risk factors apply. "Capital Markets Product Tokens" or "CMPTs" means any token or digital asset: (i) whose value, pricing, or yield characteristics are derived from, referenced to, or structured with reference to any listed or unlisted equity security, debt security, fund unit, derivative, index, or other capital markets instrument (each, a "Reference Instrument"); or (ii) which is marketed, described, or otherwise presented as tracking, replicating, representing, or providing economic exposure to the performance of any such Reference Instrument, regardless of the legal structure, method of issuance, jurisdiction of issuance, or characterisation of the token: (a) Nature and legal characterisation. The legal characterisation of a CMPT may vary across jurisdictions and may differ from its economic description or marketing. A CMPT may or may not constitute a security, debt obligation, derivative, or other regulated financial instrument in any given jurisdiction. You should obtain independent legal and financial advice as to the characterisation of any CMPT before transacting; (b) No shareholder rights or beneficial interest. Holding a CMPT may not grant you any legal or beneficial rights in, or against, the issuer of its Reference Instrument. You may have no voting rights, no entitlement to shareholder or bondholder communications, and no ability to bring claims on behalf of the issuer of the Reference Instrument. Your rights as a holder of a CMPT are determined solely by the terms of the relevant token and applicable issuer documentation, which may change; (c) Distributions and corporate actions. Distributions payable in respect of a Reference Instrument (including dividends, interest, and other income) may not be passed through to holders of a CMPT, or may be passed through in a modified or delayed form. Corporate actions affecting a Reference Instrument (including splits, consolidations, mergers, spin-offs, or rights issues) may be reflected in CMPTs through adjustments determined at the issuer's discretion. The economic effect of any such adjustment may differ materially from the effect on a direct holder of the Reference Instrument; (d) Regulatory restrictions. Such restrictions may apply regardless of prevailing market conditions or the performance of the Reference Instrument. Pendle has no control over, and accepts no responsibility for, any restrictions on transferability or redeemability imposed by issuers or third parties; (f) Issuer and counterparty risk. Your rights as a holder of a CMPT may be rights against the issuer of that token rather than in respect of the Reference Instrument. An issuer of a CMPT may not be regulated in all relevant jurisdictions, and its obligations may not be guaranteed by any governmental authority or financial institution. In the event of an issuer's insolvency, operational failure, or default, you may recover less than the face value of the token, or nothing; (g) Tracking and basis risk. A CMPT may not track the performance of its Reference Instrument precisely or at all times. The value of a CMPT may diverge materially from the market price of its Reference Instrument due to factors including liquidity constraints, funding costs, structural adjustments, or market microstructure conditions. You should not assume that a CMPT's return profile is equivalent to that of holding the Reference Instrument directly; (h) Structural and synthetic risk. A CMPT may behave differently from its Reference Instrument, including under stressed, illiquid, or unusual market conditions. The structural characteristics of a CMPT may give rise to risks that are not present in direct holdings of the Reference Instrument, and its value may be affected by factors unrelated to the performance of the Reference Instrument; (i) Compounded risk within the Protocol. When CMPTs are used as yield-bearing assets within the Protocol, you are exposed to all risks described elsewhere in these Terms in addition to the risks in this section. These risks may compound, and your aggregate risk exposure when using CMPTs within the Protocol may be materially greater than when using other yield-bearing assets; and (j) Regulatory and legal uncertainty. The regulatory characterisation of CMPTs may be uncertain, may vary across jurisdictions, and may change without notice. Regulatory or legal developments may adversely affect the legality, tradability, value, or availability of CMPTs. Pendle has no control over any issuer's regulatory compliance and makes no representation as to whether any CMPT complies with the laws or regulations of any jurisdiction.
